reason:
NOT REFUTED, AND THE PAGE SURVIVES AN ATTACK THAT VERY NEARLY BROKE IT.

I downloaded the full OCR of Rosenthal's volume 2 (archive.org item THEMUQADDIMAHOFIBNKHALDUNVOLUME2) and worked from it, not from the verifier's summary. Two independent witnesses inside the book:

1. The printed table of contents lists the section between its neighbours, at '[40] Curtailment of the allowances given by the ruler implies curtailment of the tax revenue 102', then 'Injustice brings about the ruin of civilization 103', then 'How it happens that access to the ruler becomes restricted in the dynasty 111'. The section number is mangled by the OCR in the contents but is legible as 41 in the body.

2. The body text: 'This is how God proceeds with His servants. [section] 41 Injustice brings about the ruin of civilization: It should be known that attacks on people's property remove the incentive to acquire and gain property.' Rosenthal's wording is exactly the proposed wording, with a colon where the quotation takes a full stop, which is what the note says.

THE ATTACK. This scan's OCR order made me think for a while that the heading sits on page 102 and that the verifier had gained a page, which would have been a refutation. It does not. I settled the convention by testing it on two neighbouring sections whose pages the contents already fixes. Section 39 is listed at page 97, and in the OCR the marker '96' is followed by the running head 'The Dynasty's Changing Financial Status' and then the section 39 heading; section 41 is listed at 103, and the marker '102' is followed by a running head and then, further down, the section 41 heading. Both only fit if this scan emits the page number at the foot of a page and the running head at the head of the next. Under that convention section 39 lands on 97 and section 41 lands on 103, both matching the printed contents. So the locator, Chapter III, section 41, volume 2, page 103, is right, and it is right on two witnesses rather than one.

ONE THING IN THE VERIFIER'S EVIDENCE IS WRONG, AND IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE CITATION. The evidence says the running head on page 104 is 'Injustice, the Ruin of Civilization'. It is not: by the same convention, page 104's running head is 'Chapter III: Section 41' and page 105's is 'Injustice, the Ruin of Civilization'. The verifier read the heads one page early. The page of the section heading itself does not depend on that reading, because the contents page fixes it independently, so the source line needs no change. I record the error so nobody later treats that sentence of the evidence as checked.

THE REAL QUESTION, WHICH IS WHETHER A HEADING MAY SHIP. It may, and the note already says plainly what it is. The Arabic has Ibn Khaldun's own fasl title, so the heading is authorial and not an editorial invention of the translator; Rosenthal's bracketed section numbers are his, the words are Ibn Khaldun's in Rosenthal's English. The note states three things a reader is owed, and states them correctly: that it is the printed heading of section 41, that it introduces the section rather than standing in its body, and that the terminal stop replaces the colon that follows it in the text. Nothing is hidden and nothing is minted. The fame test is met by rule 2's third clause: it is the sentence Ibn Khaldun's political economy is known by and is the standard reference point for it.

EVERY OTHER TEST. shipped.js on the exact wording with 'Ibn Khaldun': shipped [], near [], yearCount 0, not at cap, not banned. He appears once in the month's verdict directory, so nobody is doubled. Scope is clear: 1377, translation 1958, so not scripture, not film, not lyric, not proverb, not business, not oratory, nothing after 1999. There is no speaker to name. Nothing needs a content warning; the section's body is about incentives and property, and the quotation is a single abstract sentence. Tag Philosophy is the honest choice from the closed vocabulary for a work of the philosophy of history; none of the other six fits better. The quotation ends in a full stop, holds no quotation marks, is prose and is kept as prose. The source line leads with the author's name, carries no dash, and is 120 characters, inside the 140. And it is a fourteenth-century Maghrebi voice in a month that would otherwise be mostly European, saying the month's theme from the other end: not what justice builds, but what its absence costs. Ship it.
